NLP methodology
textPreview: NLP methodology

text: Each stage reuses techniques from experiments 2 through 10.
textPreview: Each stage reuses techniques from experiments 2 through 10.

text:
Experiments 2-3   Tokenize, clean, remove stopwords, and lemmatize

Experiments 4, 6, 7   POS-tag words and form noun-phrase candidates

Experiment 8   Add supporting entity labels with spaCy

Experiments 5, 9   Rank unigrams, bigrams, and trigrams with TF-IDF

Experiment 9   Compare resume and job text with cosine similarity

Experiment 10   Summarize categories, resume lengths, and common terms

Conclusion and limitations
textPreview: Conclusion and limitations

text: Conclusion
textPreview: Conclusion

text: The app turns unstructured resume text into ranked keywords and skill matches. It can support an initial review, while keeping the steps visible and explainable.
textPreview: The app turns unstructured resume text into ranked keywords and skill matches. It can support an initial review, while keeping the steps ...

text: Limitations
textPreview: Limitations

text: The skill list is limited. TF-IDF and cosine similarity depend on shared words, not meaning. spaCy may mislabel skills, and encoding artifacts remain in some resumes. Results need human review; no accuracy evaluation was performed.
textPreview: The skill list is limited. TF-IDF and cosine similarity depend on shared words, not meaning. spaCy may mislabel skills, and encoding arti...

text: Similarity is a text comparison, not a candidate-fit probability.
textPreview: Similarity is a text comparison, not a candidate-fit probability.

text: Limitations are based on the implemented rule-based skill list, corpus-derived TF-IDF and cosine similarity, general spaCy NER, and the absence of labeled evaluation data.
